title: d- and f-Block Elements (Transition Metals, Interstitial Compounds, Lanthanoids, K2Cr2O7 & KMnO4)
syllabus: General characteristics of transition elements: electronic configurations, metallic character, melting/boiling points, enthalpy of atomization; Trends in atomic and ionic radii, variable oxidation states, standard electrode potentials (E° values), catalytic properties, colored ion formation, and magnetic moments (spin-only formula); Formation of interstitial compounds and alloy formation; Preparation, properties, structures, and oxidizing action of potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7) and potassium permanganate (KMnO4) in acidic, neutral, and alkaline media; Chromyl chloride test; f-Block elements: Lanthanoids (electronic configuration, +3 oxidation state and exceptions, lanthanoid contraction and its consequences) and Actinoids (general characteristics, comparison with lanthanoids)

title: p-Block Elements: Groups 15 to 18 (Allotropy, Trends in Reactivity, & Group Chemistry)
syllabus: Group 15 elements (Nitrogen family): Electronic configuration, trends in atomic/ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electronegativity; Oxidation states and inert pair effect; Anomalous behavior of nitrogen (catenation, multiple bonding); Allotropes of phosphorus (white, red, black); Hydrides, oxides, and oxoacids of nitrogen and phosphorus; Group 16 elements (Oxygen family): Trends in physical properties, anomalous properties of oxygen; Allotropes of sulfur (rhombic, monoclinic, plastic); Oxides, oxoacids of sulfur (sulfurous, sulfuric, peroxodisulfuric, thiosulfuric); Group 17 elements (Halogens): Trends in electronegativity, electron gain enthalpy (F vs Cl anomaly), bond dissociation enthalpy (Cl2 > Br2 > F2 > I2); Anomalous behavior of fluorine; Interhalogen compounds and oxoacids; Group 18 elements (Noble gases): General properties, ionization enthalpies, Bartlett's experiment; Compounds of xenon (fluorides: XeF2, XeF4, XeF6; oxides/oxyfluorides: XeO3, XeOF4, XeO2F2) - preparations, structures, geometries, and hydrolysis

title: p-Block Elements: Group 13 & 14 (Electronic Configurations, Oxidation States, & Anomalous Properties)
syllabus: Group 13 elements (Boron family: B, Al, Ga, In, Tl): General characteristics, electronic configurations, atomic and ionic radii, ionization enthalpies, and electronegativity; Inert pair effect and stability of +1 vs +3 oxidation states; Anomalous properties and diagonal relationship of boron with silicon; Electron-deficient nature, Lewis acidity of boron trihalides, structure and 3c-2e bonding in diborane (B2H6); Borax bead test, orthoboric acid (H3BO3) and its Lewis acidic behavior; Amphoteric character of Al and Ga oxides/hydroxides; Group 14 elements (Carbon family: C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb): General trends, catenation, multiple bonding (pπ-pπ vs pπ-dπ), allotropes of carbon (diamond, graphite, fullerenes, graphene); Inert pair effect and relative stabilities of +2 vs +4 oxidation states (Sn and Pb redox behavior); Anomalous behavior of carbon; Oxides of carbon (CO, CO2), silicates and silicones structures and classifications

title: VSEPR & Hybridization (Valence Bond Theory, Orbital Overlapping, & Molecular Geometries)
syllabus: Valence Bond Theory (VBT), directional nature of covalent bonds; Orbital overlapping: head-on (axial) and lateral (sideways) overlaps, sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds, relative strengths of bonds; Concept of hybridization: sp, sp², sp³, sp³d, sp³d², sp³d³ hybrid orbitals; Resonance and formal charges; Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory: postulates, electron-pair repulsions (lp-lp > lp-bp > bp-bp); Determination of steric number; Prediction of shapes and molecular geometries of molecules and polyatomic ions (linear, bent, trigonal planar, pyramidal, T-shaped, see-saw, square planar, square pyramidal, pentagonal bipyramidal); Bond angles, deviations from ideal angles, and Bent's rule

title: Trigonometry, Inverse Trig, & Statistics
syllabus: Trigonometric identities, compound, multiple, and sub-multiple angle formulas; General solution and trigonometric equations; Inverse trigonometric functions: principal value branches, domain, range, and operational properties; Measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and dispersion (mean deviation, variance, standard deviation) for grouped and ungrouped data; Effect of linear transformations on mean and variance

title: Thermodynamics: First Law (System, State Functions, Work, Heat, & Internal Energy)
syllabus: Concepts of system and surroundings; Types of systems (open, closed, and isolated); State variables and state functions vs path functions; Intensive and extensive properties; Thermodynamic processes (isothermal, adiabatic, isobaric, isochoric, cyclic, reversible, and irreversible); Internal energy (U) as a state function; Heat (q) and work (w), sign conventions according to IUPAC; First law of thermodynamics (ΔU = q + w); Pressure-volume work (w = -P_ext ΔV, reversible isothermal expansion w = -2.303 nRT log(V2/V1)); Enthalpy (H = U + PV), relation between ΔH and ΔU (ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT); Heat capacities: C, C_m, C_p, and C_v, relation between C_p and C_v (Mayer's formula: C_p - C_v = R); Adiabatic processes for ideal gases (PV^γ = const, TV^(γ-1) = const)

title: Thermochemistry & Spontaneity (Second Law, Entropy, & Gibbs Free Energy)
syllabus: Second law of thermodynamics; Spontaneous and non-spontaneous processes; Entropy (S) as a state function and measure of randomness; Entropy changes for reversible and irreversible processes, phase transitions, and ideal gas expansions (ΔS = n C_v ln(T2/T1) + n R ln(V2/V1)); Total entropy change (ΔS_total = ΔS_system + ΔS_surroundings) and criteria for spontaneity; Gibbs free energy (G = H - TS) and Gibbs-Helmholtz equation; Criteria for spontaneity at constant temperature and pressure (ΔG < 0); Effect of temperature on reaction spontaneity; Standard Gibbs energy change (ΔG°) and its relationship to equilibrium constant (K_eq); Third law of thermodynamics and absolute entropies

title: Redox Reactions (Oxidation Numbers & Balancing Redox Equations)
syllabus: Concept of oxidation and reduction; Redox reactions in terms of electron transfer; Oxidation number rules, fractional and exceptional oxidation numbers (CrO5, H2SO5, Fe3O4, C3O2, Br3O8, S4O6^2-); Types of redox reactions: combination, decomposition, displacement, and disproportionation/comproportionation; Balancing redox reactions by ion-electron (half-reaction) method and oxidation state method in acidic and alkaline media; Calculation of n-factor (valency factor) and equivalent mass for oxidizing and reducing agents; Redox titrations (permanganometry, dichromometry, iodometry, iodimetry)

title: Quantum Mechanical Model of Atom
syllabus: Schrödinger wave equation (qualitative treatment); Significance of wave function (ψ) and probability density (ψ²); Quantum numbers (principal, azimuthal, magnetic, and spin) and their physical significance; Shapes of s, p, d, and f orbitals; Radial and angular wave functions, radial probability distribution curves, radial and angular nodes; Rules for filling electrons in orbitals: Aufbau principle, Pauli's exclusion principle, Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity; Electronic configuration of elements, anomalous configurations (Cr, Cu, etc.), exchange energy and stability of half-filled and completely filled subshells

title: Quantum Mechanical Model (Quantum Numbers, Orbitals, & Shapes of s, p, and d Orbitals)
syllabus: Quantum mechanical model of atom: Schrödinger wave equation (qualitative concept), wave function (ψ), physical significance of probability density (|ψ|²); Concept of atomic orbital; Quantum numbers: Principal (n), Azimuthal / Orbital angular momentum (l), Magnetic (m_l), and Spin (m_s); Energy levels, subshells, and spatial orientation of orbitals; Shapes of atomic orbitals: s (spherical), p (dumb-bell), d (double dumb-bell and d_z² with ring); Radial and angular wave functions; Nodes: Radial nodes (n - l - 1), Angular nodes (l), and Total nodes (n - 1); Nodal planes and nodal surfaces; Degeneracy of orbitals; Orbital angular momentum (L = √[l(l+1)] ħ); Spin magnetic moment (μ_s = √[n(n+2)] BM); Rules for filling electrons in orbitals: Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, and Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity; Electronic configurations of atoms and exceptional configurations (Cr, Cu)

title: Periodic Properties (Modern Periodic Law, Radii, IE, Electron Gain Enthalpy, & Electronegativity)
syllabus: Modern periodic law and the present form of the periodic table; s, p, d, and f block elements; Periodic trends in physical and chemical properties: Atomic and ionic radii (covalent, van der Waals, and metallic radii), lanthanoid contraction; Isoelectronic species and radii comparison; Ionization enthalpy (IE1, IE2, IE3), factors affecting IE, successive ionization enthalpies, and anomalous trends (Be vs B, N vs O); Electron gain enthalpy (ΔegH) and its anomalies (F vs Cl, O vs S, noble gases, alkaline earth metals); Electronegativity scales (Pauling and Mulliken) and its periodic trends; Periodic anomalies and diagonal relationships

title: Organic Intermediates & Mechanisms (Carbocations, Carbanions, Free Radicals, & Acid-Base Analysis)
syllabus: Homolytic and heterolytic bond fission; Generation, geometry, electronic structure, and relative stabilities of reactive intermediates: carbocations (classical and non-classical, cyclopropylmethyl cation, allylic, benzylic, tropylium), carbanions, free radicals, carbenes (singlet and triplet), and nitrenes; Carbocation rearrangements: 1,2-hydride shift, 1,2-methyl/alkyl shift, ring expansion, and ring contraction; Electrophiles and nucleophiles (ambident nucleophiles, hard and soft nucleophiles); Quantitative and qualitative acidity analysis: carboxylic acids, substituted benzoic acids, phenols, alcohols, active methylene compounds; Basicity analysis: aliphatic amines (solvent, inductive, and steric effects), aromatic amines, amidines, guanidine, pyrrole vs pyridine; Nucleophilicity vs basicity; Electrophilic, nucleophilic, and radical reaction mechanisms overview

title: Nernst Equation & Batteries (Nernst Equation Applications, Gibbs Energy, Fuel Cells, & Corrosion Mechanics)
syllabus: Nernst equation and its applications to half-cells and full galvanic cells; Concentration dependence of electrode potentials and cell EMF; Calculation of cell potential, reaction quotient (Q), and equilibrium constant (K); Relationship between cell potential, standard cell potential, and thermodynamic parameters (ΔG, ΔG°, ΔH, ΔS, and temperature coefficient of EMF (∂E/∂T)_P); Commercial batteries: Primary batteries (dry cell / Leclanché cell, mercury button cell) and secondary batteries (lead-acid storage battery, nickel-cadmium storage cell); Charging and discharging chemistry; Fuel cells: Hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell (design, reactions, and thermodynamic efficiency); Corrosion as an electrochemical phenomenon: Mechanism of rusting of iron, factors affecting corrosion, and methods of prevention (cathodic protection, sacrificial anodes, galvanization, and barrier protection)

title: Nature of Matter & Laws (Atomic Mass, Molecular Mass, & Laws of Chemical Combination)
syllabus: Nature of matter, elements, compounds, and mixtures; Physical and chemical properties of matter and their measurement (SI units, significant figures, precision and accuracy, scientific notation, dimensional analysis); Dalton's atomic theory, atomic and molecular masses, average atomic mass, formula mass, unified mass (u / amu); Laws of chemical combination: Law of conservation of mass (Lavoisier), Law of definite/constant proportions (Proust), Law of multiple proportions (Dalton), Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes, Avogadro's law and molecular hypothesis; Calculation of average isotopic mass, percentage abundance, and basic quantitative problems based on combination laws

title: Molecular Orbital Theory (LCAO Method, MOT Diagrams, Bond Order, & Magnetic Behavior)
syllabus: Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT) and its fundamental features; Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals (LCAO) approximation: conditions for combination of atomic orbitals, bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals; Sigma (σ), Pi (π), and Delta (δ) molecular orbitals, symmetry and nodal planes (gerade and ungerade orbitals); Molecular orbital energy level diagrams for homonuclear diatomic molecules with total electrons ≤ 14 (with s-p mixing: B2, C2, N2) and > 14 (without s-p mixing: O2, F2, Ne2); Electronic configuration of homonuclear and heteronuclear diatomic species (CO, NO, CN-, NO+); Calculation of bond order (BO = 1/2(Nb - Na)); Prediction of magnetic properties (paramagnetism and diamagnetism); Comparison of relative stabilities, bond lengths, and bond dissociation energies of diatomic molecules and their ions (O2, O2+, O2-, O2^2-, N2, N2+, N2-)

title: Mole Concept & Stoichiometry (Empirical & Molecular Formulas, Stoichiometric Calculations)
syllabus: Mole concept, Avogadro constant, molar mass; Percentage composition of elements in compounds; Empirical and molecular formulas from elemental analysis and vapor density; Stoichiometry and stoichiometric calculations based on balanced chemical equations; Limiting reagent and excess reactant; Calculation of theoretical yield, actual yield, and percentage yield; Quantitative problems involving reactions in solutions (Molarity, Molality, Mole fraction, Mass percentage, and ppm); Gas stoichiometry at STP and NTP

title: Mole Concept & Stoichiometry
syllabus: Matter and its nature, Dalton's atomic theory; Concept of atom, molecule, element, and compound; Laws of chemical combination; Atomic and molecular masses, mole concept, molar mass, percentage composition; Empirical and molecular formulas; Chemical equations and stoichiometry, limiting reagent, sequential and parallel reactions

title: Liquid Solutions (Vapour Pressure, Raoult's Law, Ideal & Non-Ideal Solutions)
syllabus: Vapour pressure of liquid solutions; Raoult's Law for volatile solutes (binary liquid-liquid mixtures) and non-volatile solutes; Dalton's Law of partial pressures and vapor phase composition (Dalton-Raoult combined relationship); Bubble point and dew point equations; Ideal solutions (thermodynamic criteria: ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0, ΔS_mix > 0, ΔG_mix < 0); Non-ideal solutions showing positive and negative deviations from Raoult's Law (intermolecular forces, thermodynamic signatures); Azeotropic mixtures (minimum and maximum boiling azeotropes); Fractional distillation and boiling-point composition diagrams

title: Ionic Equilibrium (Electrolytes, pH Scale, Ostwald's Dilution Law, & Common Ion Effect)
syllabus: Electrolytes and non-electrolytes, strong and weak electrolytes; Arrhenius, Brønsted-Lowry, and Lewis concepts of acids and bases; Ionization of weak acids and weak bases, Ostwald's dilution law; Degree of ionization (α) and ionization constants (Ka and Kb); Self-ionization of water, ionic product of water (Kw), effect of temperature on Kw; pH and pOH scale, relationship between pH, pOH, and pKw; Calculation of pH for strong and weak monoprotic and polyprotic acids and bases; Common ion effect and suppression of ionization; Mixture of strong and weak acids/bases

title: Indefinite Integration (Substitution, By Parts, and Partial Fractions)
syllabus: Fundamental formulas and basic properties of indefinite integrals; Integration by algebraic, trigonometric, and hyperbolic substitutions; Integration by parts, ILATE rule, and integrals of the form ∫e^x [f(x) + f'(x)] dx; Integration of rational functions using partial fractions; Standard integrals involving quadratic expressions in the denominator (with and without square root); Integrals of trigonometric forms like ∫dx/(a + b cos x), ∫(a sin x + b cos x)/(c sin x + d cos x) dx, and algebraic twins ∫(x^2 ± 1)/(x^4 + kx^2 + 1) dx

title: Hydrolysis & Buffers (Salt Hydrolysis, Buffer Solutions, and Solubility Product)
syllabus: Hydrolysis of salts of different types (strong acid-weak base, weak acid-strong base, weak acid-weak base); Degree of hydrolysis (h), hydrolysis constant (Kh), and pH calculations of salt solutions; Buffer solutions: acidic and basic buffers, mechanism of buffer action, Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, buffer capacity, and buffer range; Solubility equilibria of sparingly soluble salts; Solubility product (Ksp), relationship between solubility (s) and Ksp, common ion effect on solubility, simultaneous solubility, ionic product (Qsp) and condition for precipitation

title: Hydrocarbons (Alkanes Conformations, Alkenes Additions, Ozonolysis, & Aromatic Substitution)
syllabus: Alkanes: Conformations of ethane and n-butane (Newman and Sawhorse projections, dihedral angles, torsional and steric strain, relative stability); Free radical halogenation of alkanes (reactivity vs selectivity, mechanism); Alkenes: Structure, geometrical isomerism; Electrophilic addition reactions (addition of hydrogen halides, Markovnikov's rule, carbocation rearrangements); Peroxide effect (Kharasch effect / Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr, radical mechanism, why HCl and HI fail); Hydration (acid-catalyzed, oxymercuration-demercuration, hydroboration-oxidation); Ozonolysis (reductive vs oxidative cleavage, structure elucidation of alkenes and alkynes); Oxidation with cold dilute alkaline KMnO4 (Baeyer's reagent) and hot acidic KMnO4; Alkynes: Acidity of terminal alkynes, addition reactions, hydration (Kucherov's reaction); Aromatic Hydrocarbons: Benzene structure, aromaticity; Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (EAS) mechanisms (halogenation, nitration, sulfonation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation); Directive influence and activating/deactivating effects of functional groups, side-chain oxidations

title: General Organic Chemistry (IUPAC, Isomerism, & Electronic Effects)
syllabus: IUPAC nomenclature of polyfunctional organic compounds, bicyclic and spiro compounds; Structural isomerism (chain, position, functional, metamerism, and tautomerism - keto-enol, triad systems, factors affecting enol content); Stereoisomerism: Geometrical isomerism (cis-trans, E-Z notation, conditions for GI, number of geometrical isomers), Optical isomerism (chirality, enantiomers, diastereomers, meso compounds, R/S configuration, optical activity, Fischer and Newman projections); Electronic displacements in covalent bonds: Inductive effect (+I and -I effects, applications to acid/base strength), Electromeric effect, Resonance effect and Mesomeric effect (+M and -M, rules of resonance, resonance energy), Hyperconjugation (Baker-Nathan effect, no-bond resonance, stability of carbocations, carbon radicals, and alkenes, heat of hydrogenation); Relative stabilities of reactive intermediates (carbocations, carbanions, free radicals, carbenes); Aromaticity (Hückel's 4n+2 rule, antiaromatic, non-aromatic systems); Acidity and basicity comparison of organic acids, phenols, carboxylic acids, and amines (ortho effect, SIR, SIP)

title: Functional Groups (Alkyl Halides, Alcohols, Phenols, Aldehydes, & Ketones)
syllabus: Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic substitution mechanisms (SN1 vs SN2 kinetics, stereochemistry, Walden inversion vs racemization, substrate reactivity, solvent and leaving group effects), elimination reactions (E1 and E2); Alcohols: Preparation, acidic character, distinction tests (Lucas test, Victor Meyer test), dehydration of alcohols (carbocation rearrangement, Zaitsev alkene formation), pinacol-pinacolone rearrangement; Phenols: Acidity, Kolbe's reaction, Reimer-Tiemann reaction (intermediate and mechanism), reaction with Zn dust, electrophilic substitutions (bromination, nitration); Aldehydes and Ketones: Nucleophilic addition reactions (addition of HCN, NaHSO3, Grignard reagents, alcohols, and ammonia derivatives), reactivity comparison toward nucleophilic attack; Alpha-hydrogen reactivity: Aldol condensation, cross-aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction and cross-Cannizzaro reaction, haloform test (iodoform reaction)

title: Entropy & Spontaneity (Second Law of Thermodynamics, Entropy, Gibbs Energy, & Equilibrium Criteria)
syllabus: Spontaneous and non-spontaneous processes; Limitations of the First Law of Thermodynamics; Second Law of Thermodynamics; Concept of entropy (S) as a measure of disorder/randomness; State function nature of entropy; Calculation of entropy change (ΔS = q_rev / T); Entropy changes in phase transitions (fusion, vaporization, sublimation) and Trouton's rule; Entropy changes during expansion/compression of ideal gases; Total entropy change of system and surroundings (ΔS_total = ΔS_sys + ΔS_surr) as criterion for spontaneity; Gibbs free energy (G = H - TS); Gibbs energy change (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS) and Gibbs-Helmholtz equation; Criteria for spontaneity and equilibrium under conditions of constant T and P (ΔG < 0 for spontaneity, ΔG = 0 for equilibrium, ΔG > 0 for non-spontaneous); Effect of temperature on reaction spontaneity (signs of ΔH and ΔS); Standard Gibbs free energy change (ΔrG°) and its relation to the equilibrium constant K (ΔrG° = -2.303 RT log K); Third Law of Thermodynamics and absolute entropies (residual entropy concept)

title: Enthalpies & Hess's Law (Enthalpy of Reaction, Formation, Combustion, Atomisation, Sublimation, & Hess's Law)
syllabus: Enthalpy change of a reaction (ΔrH); Standard enthalpy changes (standard state definitions); Types of enthalpy changes: Standard enthalpy of formation (ΔfH°), Standard enthalpy of combustion (ΔcH°), Enthalpy of atomisation (ΔaH°), Enthalpy of phase transitions (sublimation ΔsubH°, fusion ΔfusH°, vaporization ΔvapH° and their relationships); Bond dissociation enthalpy and mean bond enthalpy; Enthalpy of solution (ΔsolH°) and hydration enthalpy (ΔhydH°); Enthalpy of neutralisation (strong acid - strong base vs weak acid/base); Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation and its applications; Born-Haber cycle for lattice enthalpy determination; Temperature dependence of enthalpy of reaction (Kirchhoff's equation - qualitative/quantitative)

title: Electronic Configurations (Aufbau Principle, Pauli Exclusion, Hund's Rule, & Subshell Stability)
syllabus: Rules for filling of electrons in atomic orbitals: Aufbau principle (building-up principle) and the (n + l) energy ranking rule; Pauli's exclusion principle and maximum orbital occupancy; Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity, electron pairing, and exchange interactions; Ground state vs excited state electron configurations; Exceptional electronic configurations in the periodic table (Cr, Cu, Pd, Pt, Au, etc.); Electronic configurations of cations and anions (transition metal ionizations, order of electron removal from ns vs (n-1)d); Origin of extra stability of completely filled and half-filled subshells: symmetrical spatial distribution of electron density and maximum exchange energy; Calculation of number of exchange pairs; Magnetic properties: diamagnetic vs paramagnetic species, calculation of spin-only magnetic moments (μ = √[n(n+2)] BM)

title: Dual Nature & Uncertainty (Matter Waves, de Broglie Relation, & Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle)
syllabus: Dual nature of matter and radiation; de Broglie wavelength relation (λ = h/p = h/mv = h/√(2mE) = h/√(2mqV)); de Broglie wavelength for microscopic vs macroscopic objects; Derivation and connection of de Broglie hypothesis with Bohr's quantization condition (2πr = nλ); Experimental verification of wave nature of electrons (Davisson-Germer experiment - qualitative); Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle (Δx · Δp ≥ h/4π, Δx · Δv ≥ h/4πm); Energy-time uncertainty relationship (ΔE · Δt ≥ h/4π); Physical significance and conceptual implications of uncertainty principle; Inapplicability of definite circular trajectories / Bohr orbits; Significance of uncertainty principle for macroscopic vs microscopic particles; Conceptual and numerical problem-solving for NEET

title: Differential Equations
syllabus: Order and degree of a differential equation; Formation of differential equations; Solutions of first order and first degree differential equations by the method of separation of variables; Solution of homogeneous differential equations (y = vx substitution); Solution of linear differential equations of the type dy/dx + Py = Q and dx/dy + Px = Q; Integrating factor (I.F.); Initial value problems and orthogonal trajectories/curve families

title: Definite Integration (Properties of Definite Integrals and Wallis' Formula)
syllabus: Fundamental theorem of calculus; Basic properties of definite integrals (King's property, Queen's property, even and odd functions, periodic properties); Evaluation of definite integrals involving greatest integer, modulus, and fractional part functions; Wallis' formulas and reduction formulas for trigonometric powers; Leibniz rule of differentiation under the integral sign; Definite integral as the limit of a Riemann sum

title: Coordination Chemistry Basics (Werner's Theory, Ligands, IUPAC Nomenclature, & Isomerism)
syllabus: Werner's coordination theory: Primary and secondary valencies, precipitation and conductance studies; Definitions: Coordination entity, central atom/ion, coordination number, coordination sphere, and counter ions; Ligands: Monodentate, bidentate, polydentate, chelating ligands, ambidentate ligands and linkage isomerism, denticity and chelate effect; IUPAC nomenclature of mononuclear coordination compounds; Isomerism in coordination compounds: Structural isomerism (ionization, hydrate/solvate, linkage, coordination isomerism) and Stereoisomerism (geometrical isomerism in square planar [MA2B2, MA2BC, MABCD] and octahedral complexes [MA4B2, MA3B3 - fac/mer], optical isomerism, enantiomers, and plane of symmetry)

title: Conductance & Galvanic Cells (Molar Conductivity, Kohlrausch’s Law, Electrochemical Cells, & EMF Calculation)
syllabus: Electrolytic conduction, resistance, conductance, resistivity, conductivity (specific conductance κ), cell constant; Molar conductivity (Λm), equivalent conductivity, variation of conductivity and molar conductivity with concentration for strong and weak electrolytes; Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation; Kohlrausch’s law of independent migration of ions and its applications (limiting molar conductivity, degree of dissociation α, dissociation constant Ka, solubility of sparingly soluble salts); Galvanic (voltaic) cells, Daniell cell, half-cell reactions, cell notation, salt bridge and its functions; Standard electrode potentials, SHE (standard hydrogen electrode), electrochemical series; Nernst equation for electrode potential and cell EMF; Equilibrium constant (Keq) and Gibbs free energy change (ΔG° = -nFE°cell); Concentration cells

title: Concentration Terms (Molarity, Molality, Mole Fraction, Mass Percentage, & ppm)
syllabus: Methods of expressing concentration of solutions: Mass percentage (w/w), Volume percentage (v/v), Mass by volume percentage (w/v), Parts per million (ppm), Parts per billion (ppb); Mole fraction (X), Molarity (M), Molality (m), Normality (N), Formality; Temperature dependence of concentration terms (temperature-dependent vs temperature-independent units); Dilution law and mixing of solutions (M1V1 = M2V2, M_mix = (M1V1 + M2V2)/(V1 + V2)); Interconversion between concentration terms (Molarity to Molality, Mole fraction to Molality, Mass percent and density to Molarity); Standard solutions and quantitative solution stoichiometry

title: Concentration Terms
syllabus: Solutions and concentration expressions; Mass percentage (% w/w), volume percentage (% v/v), and mass by volume percentage (% w/v); Parts per million (ppm); Mole fraction; Molarity (M) and effect of temperature; Molality (m) and temperature independence; Normality (N) and n-factor (valency factor); Interconversions between concentration terms (Molarity to Molality, % w/w to Molarity); Dilution law and mixing of non-reacting solutions

title: Collision & Arrhenius Theory (Half-Life, Temperature Dependence, & Activation Energy)
syllabus: Collision theory of chemical reactions: Collision frequency (Z), steric/orientation factor (P), and effective collisions; Transition state theory and potential energy profile diagrams (activation energy of forward and backward reactions, threshold energy, reaction enthalpy ΔH); Arrhenius equation (k = A e^(-Ea/RT)), linear logarithmic forms (ln k vs 1/T, log10 k vs 1/T); Temperature coefficient of reaction rate; Calculation of activation energy (Ea) and frequency factor (A); Effect of positive and negative catalysts on activation energy and reaction coordinates; Half-life variations and temperature-dependent multi-step kinetics

title: Colligative Properties & van 't Hoff Factor
syllabus: Colligative properties of dilute solutions; Relative lowering of vapour pressure (RLVP) and determination of molar mass; Elevation of boiling point (ebullioscopy) and molal elevation constant (K_b); Depression of freezing point (cryoscopy) and molal depression constant (K_f); Thermodynamic derivation and physical significance of K_b and K_f; Osmosis, osmotic pressure (π = iCRT), isotonic, hypertonic, and hypotonic solutions, and reverse osmosis; Abnormal molar masses and van 't Hoff factor (i); Degree of dissociation (α) and degree of association (β)

title: Classical Thermodynamics (First Law, Work, Heat, Internal Energy, Enthalpy, & Hess's Law)
syllabus: Fundamentals of thermodynamics: System and surroundings, extensive and intensive properties, state and path functions; First law of thermodynamics: Internal energy (U), heat (q), and work (w); Pressure-volume work in reversible and irreversible isothermal/adiabatic expansions and compressions of ideal gases; Enthalpy (H), relation between ΔH and ΔU (ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT); Heat capacities (C_p, C_v) and their relationship; Thermochemistry: Standard enthalpy changes of reaction, formation, combustion, neutralization, and phase transitions; Hess's Law of constant heat summation and its applications; Bond dissociation enthalpies and lattice enthalpy (Born-Haber cycle)

title: Chemical Kinetics (Rate Law, Order, Molecularity, & Integrated Rate Equations)
syllabus: Rate of a chemical reaction (average and instantaneous rate); Factors affecting the rate of reaction: concentration, temperature, pressure, and catalyst; Rate law expression and specific rate constant (k); Order and molecularity of elementary and complex reactions; Units of rate constant for nth order reactions; Integrated rate laws and half-life expressions for zero-order and first-order reactions; Graphical representations of zero and first-order kinetics; Pseudo-first-order reactions (inversion of cane sugar, hydrolysis of esters); Methods for determining reaction order (initial rates method, integrated rate method, half-life method)

title: Chemical Equilibrium Basics (Law of Mass Action, Equilibrium Constant, & Le Chatelier's Principle)
syllabus: Equilibrium in physical and chemical processes, dynamic nature of equilibrium; Law of mass action and equilibrium constant (Kc and Kp); Relationship between Kp and Kc (Kp = Kc(RT)^Δng); Characteristics of equilibrium constant and units; Reaction quotient (Qc and Qp) and prediction of direction of reaction; Homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria; Factors affecting equilibrium (Le Chatelier's principle): effect of concentration, pressure, volume, temperature (van 't Hoff equation), addition of inert gas (at constant volume and constant pressure), and effect of catalyst; Relation between Gibbs energy change (ΔG) and equilibrium constant (ΔrG° = -RT ln K)

title: Chemical Equilibrium (Law of Mass Action, Kp and Kc, & Le Chatelier's Principle)
syllabus: Dynamic nature of equilibrium, Law of mass action and equilibrium constants (K_c and K_p); Relation between K_p and K_c (K_p = K_c(RT)^Δn_g); Characteristics and thermodynamic interpretation of equilibrium constant; Reaction quotient (Q) and predicting the direction of reaction; Homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria; Degree of dissociation (α) and vapor density measurements; Factors affecting equilibrium (Le Chatelier's principle): effect of concentration, pressure, volume, temperature, and addition of inert gas at constant volume/pressure; van 't Hoff equation

title: Chemical Bonding Basics (Kossel-Lewis Approach, Ionic Bond, Lattice Enthalpy, Fajan's Rule, & Dipole Moments)
syllabus: Kossel-Lewis approach to chemical bonding; Octet rule and its limitations (expanded octet, electron-deficient molecules, odd-electron species); Ionic (electrovalent) bonding: formation, factors favoring ionic bond; Lattice enthalpy, Born-Haber cycle and Kapustinskii approximation; Polarization of ions and Fajan's rules (covalent character in ionic compounds, polarizing power of cations, polarizability of anions, pseudo-noble gas electron configuration); Dipole moment (μ), Debye unit, percentage ionic character, dipole moments of polyatomic molecules and symmetric cancellation; Comparison of bond polarity (e.g., NH3 vs NF3)

title: Bonding in Coordination Compounds (VBT, CFT, CFSE, Magnetic Properties, & Color)
syllabus: Valence Bond Theory (VBT) applied to coordination complexes: Inner orbital (d2sp3, dsp2) and outer orbital (sp3d2, sp3) complexes, orbital hybridization schemes, limitations of VBT; Crystal Field Theory (CFT): Crystal field splitting in octahedral (Δo) and tetrahedral (Δt) environments, relationship between Δo and Δt (Δt = 4/9 Δo); Spectrochemical series and ligand field strength; Pairing energy (P), high-spin vs low-spin complexes for d4 to d7 configurations; Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) calculation for octahedral and tetrahedral complexes; Magnetic properties (spin-only magnetic moment formula μ = √[n(n+2)] BM); Color of coordination complexes, d-d transitions, Laporte and spin selection rules, complementary colors, Jahn-Teller distortion (qualitative), and synergic bonding in metal carbonyls

title: Atomic Structure Basics (Discovery of Subatomic Particles, Rutherford's Model, & Bohr's Hydrogen Atom)
syllabus: Discovery of subatomic particles: electron (Cathode ray experiment, J.J. Thomson e/m ratio, Millikan's oil drop experiment), proton (Anode rays/Canal rays), and neutron (Chadwick's discovery); Thomson's atomic model and its limitations; Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiment, nuclear atomic model, nuclear radius, atomic number, and mass number, limitations of Rutherford model (instability and line spectra); Dual nature of electromagnetic radiation (wave and particle nature, Planck's quantum theory, photoelectric effect); Absorption and emission line spectrum of hydrogen; Bohr's postulates for hydrogen and hydrogen-like species (He+, Li2+, Be3+): derivation and calculations of radius of Bohr orbits, velocity, kinetic/potential/total energy of electron, orbital frequency, Rydberg equation, spectral series (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund, Humphry); Limitations of Bohr's model (Zeeman effect, Stark effect, inability to explain multi-electron atoms and fine spectrum)

title: Atomic Structure (Bohr’s Model, de Broglie Relationship, & Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle)
syllabus: Bohr's model of hydrogen atom and hydrogen-like species; Postulates, radius of orbits, velocity of electron, energy states, and ionization energy; Spectral lines of hydrogen spectrum (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund series) and Rydberg equation; Dual nature of matter and radiation, de Broglie relationship; Heisenberg uncertainty principle and its physical significance; Quantum numbers and orbital angular momentum

title: Area Under Curves
syllabus: Area bounded by standard curves, lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses; Area between two intersecting curves; Area with respect to x-axis and y-axis; Regions defined by inequalities; Symmetry arguments in area computation

title: Amines, Biomolecules & Practical Analysis (Amine Basicity, Carbohydrates, Proteins, & Qualitative/Quantitative Analysis)
syllabus: Amines: Classification, preparation (reduction of nitro compounds, nitriles, amides, Gabriel phthalimide synthesis, Hoffmann bromamide degradation), physical properties, basic strength (gas phase vs aqueous solutions, steric and solvation effects), chemical reactions (carbylamine test, Hinsberg test, diazotization, azo coupling, reaction with nitrous acid); Biomolecules: Carbohydrates (classification, aldoses and ketoses, D/L-configuration, open and cyclic structures of glucose and fructose, mutarotation, glycosidic linkage, reducing and non-reducing sugars: sucrose, maltose, lactose, polysaccharides: starch and cellulose), Proteins (amino acids, zwitterion, isoelectric point, peptide bond, primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary structures, α-helix and β-pleated sheet, denaturation), Nucleic acids (chemical composition of DNA and RNA, nucleosides, nucleotides, double helix), Vitamins; Practical Organic Chemistry: Qualitative detection of extra elements (N, S, Halogens) via Lassaigne's test, detection of functional groups (unsaturation, alcoholic, phenolic, aldehydic, ketonic, carboxylic, amino), quantitative estimation (Dumas and Kjeldahl methods for nitrogen, Carius method for halogens and sulfur, Liebig method for carbon and hydrogen)

title: Vector Products (Scalar Dot Product and Vector Cross Product)
syllabus: Scalar (dot) product of vectors and its algebraic properties; Angle between two vectors; Projection of a vector on another vector or line; Condition of orthogonality; Vector (cross) product of two vectors and its properties; Geometrical interpretations of cross product (area of triangle and parallelogram); Unit vector perpendicular to two given vectors; Lagrange's identity; Scalar triple product and vector equations involving dot and cross products

title: Vector Algebra (Addition, Component Forms, and Section Formula)
syllabus: Vectors and scalars, addition of vectors, components of a vector in two and three-dimensional space, scalar multiplication, position vector of a point, dividing a line segment in a given ratio (internal and external section formula), direction cosines and direction ratios, collinearity and coplanarity of vectors using linear combinations

title: Triple Products (Scalar Triple Product and Vector Triple Product)
syllabus: Scalar triple product (STP) [a b c], geometrical interpretation as volume of parallelepiped and tetrahedron, coplanarity of three vectors, cyclic and non-cyclic permutation of vectors in STP; Vector triple product (VTP) a x (b x c) and its expansion (BAC-CAB rule), linear combinations, orthogonality conditions, and vector equations involving triple products

title: Three Dimensional Geometry (Planes)
syllabus: Equation of a plane in normal form, passing through a point and perpendicular to a given vector, passing through three non-collinear points; Intercept form of the equation of a plane; Angle between two planes; Coplanarity of two lines; Distance of a point from a plane; Distance between parallel planes; Line of intersection of two planes and family of planes passing through the intersection of two planes

title: Three Dimensional Geometry (Lines)
syllabus: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line; Vector and Cartesian equations of a line; Angle between two lines; Intersection of lines; Skew lines and shortest distance between two lines; Shortest distance between parallel lines; Foot of perpendicular and image of a point with respect to a line

title: Straight Lines
syllabus: Various forms of equations of a line (slope-intercept form, point-slope form, two-point form, intercept form, normal form); Angle between two lines and condition of parallelism and perpendicularity; Distance of a point from a line, distance between parallel lines; Foot of perpendicular and image of a point with respect to a line; Family of lines passing through the point of intersection of two lines; Centroid, incenter, and circumcenter of a triangle

title: Special Series
syllabus: Sigma notation and its algebraic properties; Sum of first n natural numbers, sum of squares and cubes of first n natural numbers; Arithmetico-Geometric Progression (AGP) and its finite/infinite summation; Method of differences; Telescoping series (partial fractions, radical forms, trigonometric forms); Miscellaneous series reducible to standard summations

title: Sets and Relations
syllabus: Sets and their representations; Union, intersection, difference, and complement of sets and their algebraic properties; Power set; Cartesian product of sets; Relations, domain, co-domain, and range of a relation; Types of relations: reflexive, symmetric, transitive, and equivalence relations

title: Sequences and Series (AP, GP, and HP)
syllabus: Arithmetic and Geometric progressions, insertion of arithmetic and geometric means between two given numbers; Relation between A.M. and G.M.; Harmonic progression (H.P.) and harmonic mean (H.M.)

title: Quadratic Equations
syllabus: Quadratic equations in real and complex number system and their solutions; Relation between roots and coefficients; Nature of roots; Formation of quadratic equations with given roots; Common roots; Symmetric functions of roots; Equations reducible to quadratic form

title: Permutations
syllabus: Fundamental principle of counting (addition and multiplication principles); Permutations as an arrangement; Meaning of P(n, r); Permutation of distinct objects; Permutations when objects are repeated; Permutations under restrictions (tie method/string method, gap method); Circular permutations (clockwise vs counter-clockwise distinctness and necklace problems)

title: Parabola (Standard Forms, Focal Chords, and Tangent Properties)
syllabus: Sections of conics, equations of conic sections (parabola) in standard forms; Focus, directrix, vertex, axis, and latus rectum; Focal distance and focal chord properties; Condition of tangency, slope form, point form, and parametric form of tangents; Points of contact; Intersection of tangents; Chord of contact

title: Monotonicity & Maxima-Minima
syllabus: Increasing and strictly increasing functions, decreasing and strictly decreasing functions; Conditions for monotonicity using first derivative; Critical points and stationary points; Local maxima and local minima, first derivative test, second derivative test; Global (absolute) maxima and minima on closed and bounded intervals; Optimization and real-world geometric applications

title: Matrices
syllabus: Matrices, algebra of matrices, type of matrices (symmetric, skew-symmetric, orthogonal, idempotent, nilpotent, involuntary), adjoint and evaluation of inverse of a square matrix using adjoint, properties of transpose, determinant of matrices, properties of adjoint and inverse of matrices

title: Limits (Indeterminate Forms, L'Hopital's Rule, and Standard Limits)
syllabus: Evaluation of limits, standard trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic limits; Indeterminate forms (0/0, infinity/infinity, 1^infinity, 0 x infinity, infinity - infinity, 0^0, infinity^0); L'Hopital's rule and its repeated applications; Series expansions (Maclaurin/Taylor) for sin x, cos x, tan x, e^x, ln(1+x), (1+x)^n; Squeeze theorem (Sandwich theorem); One-sided limits (left-hand and right-hand limits) and non-existence of limits

title: Functions
syllabus: Real-valued functions, domain, range and graph of elementary functions (polynomial, rational, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, modulus, signum, greatest integer and fractional part functions); Types of functions: into, onto (surjective), one-one (injective), many-one, and bijective functions; Composition of functions; Inverse of a function

title: Family of Straight Lines
syllabus: Family of lines passing through the point of intersection of two lines (L1 + λL2 = 0); Concurrent lines and condition for concurrency; Fixed points of parameter-dependent families; Equations of angle bisectors of two intersecting lines; Discrimination between acute and obtuse angle bisectors; Bisector containing a given point or origin

title: Ellipse and Hyperbola (Equations, Eccentricity, Directrix, and Tangents)
syllabus: Standard equations of ellipse and hyperbola; Foci, directrices, vertices, axes, eccentricity, and latus rectum; Focal properties and distances; Auxiliary circles; Tangent in slope form, point form, and parametric form; Condition of tangency; Director circle and perpendicular tangents

title: Differentiation (Chain Rule, Implicit, Parametric, and Higher-Order Derivatives)
syllabus: Derivatives of polynomial, rational, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions; Derivative of sum, difference, product, and quotient of functions; Chain rule; Derivative of implicit functions; Derivative of functions in parametric forms; Logarithmic differentiation; Second and higher-order derivatives; Differentiation of determinants and inverse functions

title: Determinants
syllabus: Determinants and their properties; Minors, cofactors, and evaluation of determinants; Area of triangles using determinants; Adjoint and evaluation of inverse of a square matrix using determinants; System of linear equations in two or three variables, testing for consistency, and solving systems of linear equations using Cramer's rule and matrix method (inverses)

title: Continuity and Differentiability
syllabus: Continuity of a function at a point and in an interval, types of discontinuities; Continuity of sum, difference, product, quotient, and composite of continuous functions; Differentiability at a point and in an interval, left-hand and right-hand derivatives; Relation between continuity and differentiability; Checking points of non-differentiability for piecewise, modulus, and greatest integer functions

title: Complex Numbers
syllabus: Complex numbers as ordered pairs of reals; Representation of complex numbers in the form a + ib and their representation in a plane; Argand diagram; Algebra of complex numbers; Modulus and argument (or amplitude) of a complex number; Square root of a complex number; Triangle inequality; Geometric representations (distance, circle, straight lines, perpendicular bisector)

title: Combinations
syllabus: Meaning of C(n, r) and its basic properties; Complementary combinations; Pascal's identity; Selection of objects (distinct and identical); Division into groups; Distribution of items; Geometric applications (number of straight lines, triangles, diagonals, intersection points); Sum of numbers formed by digits; Practical selection problems

title: Circles
syllabus: Standard forms of equations of a circle, general form of the equation of a circle, its radius and centre, equation of a circle when the endpoints of a diameter are given; Points of intersection of a line and a circle with the centre at the origin and condition for a line to be tangent to a circle; Equation of the tangent, equation of normal, and their properties

title: Binomial Theorem
syllabus: Binomial theorem for a positive integral index, general term and middle term, properties of binomial coefficients and simple applications

title: Work, Energy and Power
syllabus: Work done by a constant force and a variable force, kinetic energy, work-energy theorem, power; Notion of potential energy, potential energy of a spring, conservative and non-conservative forces, conservation of mechanical energy; Motion in a vertical circle, elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions

title: Waves
syllabus: Wave motion: Transverse and longitudinal waves, speed of wave motion; Displacement relation for a progressive wave; Principle of superposition of waves, reflection of waves; Standing waves in strings and organ pipes, fundamental mode and harmonics; Beats; Doppler effect in sound

title: Wave Optics
syllabus: Wave front and Huygens' principle, reflection and refraction of plane wave at a plane surface using wave fronts; Proof of laws of reflection and refraction using Huygens' principle; Interference, Young's double slit experiment and expression for fringe width, coherent sources and sustained interference of light; Diffraction due to a single slit, width of central maximum; Resolving power of microscopes and astronomical telescopes; Polarisation, plane polarised light, Brewster's law, uses of plane polarised light and Polaroids

title: Units and Dimensions
syllabus: Units and Measurements, System of Units, SI units, fundamental and derived units, Dimensions of physical quantities, dimensional analysis and its applications, Errors in measurement, significant figures

title: Thermodynamics
syllabus: Thermal equilibrium, Zeroth law of thermodynamics, Concept of temperature; First law of thermodynamics, Internal energy, Work done and heat absorbed in thermodynamic processes (isothermal, adiabatic, isobaric, isochoric); Cyclic and non-cyclic processes, Indicator diagrams (P-V, P-T, V-T); Second law of thermodynamics: Reversible and irreversible processes, Carnot engine and its efficiency, Heat pumps and refrigerators

title: Thermal Properties of Matter
syllabus: Heat, temperature, thermal expansion; specific heat capacity, calorimetry; change of state, latent heat capacity; Heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation, thermal conductivity, Newton's law of cooling, Stefan's law, Wien's displacement law, Green house effect

title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
syllabus: Centre of mass of a two-particle system, Centre of mass of a rigid body; Basic concepts of rotational motion; Moment of a force, torque, angular momentum, conservation of angular momentum and its applications; Moment of inertia, radius of gyration, values of moments of inertia for simple geometrical objects, parallel and perpendicular axes theorems and their applications; Rigid body rotation, equations of rotational motion, rolling motion

title: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices, and Simple Circuits
syllabus: Energy bands in solids (conductors, semiconductors, and insulators); Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, p-type and n-type semiconductors, electrical conductivity of semiconductors; p-n junction diode: formation of depletion layer and potential barrier, I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias; Diode as a rectifier (half-wave and full-wave); Special purpose p-n junction diodes: Zener diode and its characteristics, Zener diode as a voltage regulator; Optoelectronic junction devices: Photodiode, Light Emitting Diode (LED), Solar cell; Logic gates (OR, AND, NOT, NAND, NOR) and their truth tables

title: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
syllabus: Reflection of light, spherical mirrors, mirror formula; Refraction of light, total internal reflection and its applications, optical fibres; Refraction at spherical surfaces, lenses, thin lens formula, lensmaker's formula; Magnification, power of a lens, combination of thin lenses in contact; Refraction of light through a prism; Optical instruments: Microscopes and astronomical telescopes (reflecting and refracting) and their magnifying powers

title: Oscillations
syllabus: Periodic and oscillatory motions, period, frequency, displacement as a function of time, periodic functions; Simple Harmonic Motion (S.H.M.) and its equation; Phase; Oscillations of a spring: restoring force and force constant; Energy in S.H.M.: Kinetic and potential energies; Simple pendulum: derivation of expression for its time period; Free, forced and damped oscillations, resonance

title: Nuclei
syllabus: Composition and size of nucleus, atomic masses, isotopes, isobars, isotones; Mass-energy relation, mass defect, binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number; Nuclear forces and their characteristics; Nuclear fission and fusion

title: Moving Charges and Magnetism
syllabus: Biot-Savart law and its application to current carrying circular loop; Ampere's law and its applications to infinitely long straight wire and solenoid; Force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic and electric fields (Lorentz force); Motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field; Cyclotron; Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field, force between two parallel current-carrying conductors-definition of ampere; Torque experienced by a current loop in uniform magnetic field; Moving coil galvanometer-its current sensitivity and conversion to ammeter and voltmeter

title: Motion in a Straight Line
syllabus: Frame of reference, Motion in a straight line: Position-time graph, speed and velocity; Uniform and non-uniform motion, average speed and instantaneous velocity; Uniformly accelerated motion, velocity-time and position-time graphs, relations for uniformly accelerated motion; Free fall under gravity; Relative velocity in one dimension

title: Motion in a Plane
syllabus: Scalars and vectors, vector addition and subtraction, scalar and vector products, Unit vector, Resolution of a vector; Relative velocity in two dimensions, Projectile motion (horizontal and oblique), Uniform circular motion: centripetal acceleration, angular speed and velocity

title: Mechanical Properties of Solids
syllabus: Elastic behaviour, Stress-strain relationship, Hooke's law, Young's modulus, bulk modulus, modulus of rigidity, Poisson's ratio; Elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire, work done in stretching a wire

title: Mechanical Properties of Fluids
syllabus: Pressure due to a fluid column; Pascal's law and its applications (hydraulic lift and hydraulic brakes); Effect of gravity on fluid pressure; Viscosity, Stokes' law, terminal velocity, streamline and turbulent flow, critical velocity; Bernoulli's principle and its applications; Surface energy and surface tension, angle of contact, excess of pressure across a curved surface, application of surface tension ideas to drops, bubbles and capillary rise

title: Magnetism and Matter
syllabus: Current loop as a magnetic dipole and its magnetic dipole moment; Magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron; Magnetic field intensity due to a magnetic dipole (bar magnet) along its axis and perpendicular to its axis; Torque on a magnetic dipole (bar magnet) in a uniform magnetic field; Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid, magnetic field lines; Gauss's law for magnetism; Diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic substances, with examples; Electromagnets and factors affecting their strengths, permanent magnets

title: Laws of Motion Part 2: Friction & Circular Dynamics
syllabus: Static and Kinetic friction, Laws of friction, Rolling friction, Dynamics of uniform circular motion, Centripetal force and its applications, Vehicle on a level circular road, Vehicle on a banked road

title: Laws of Motion
syllabus: Newton's laws of motion, Inertia, Momentum, Impulse, Law of conservation of linear momentum and its applications, Equilibrium of concurrent forces, Static and Kinetic friction, Laws of friction, Rolling friction, Dynamics of uniform circular motion: Centripetal force and vehicle on a banked road

title: Kinetic Theory of Gases
syllabus: Equation of state of a perfect gas, work done on compressing a gas; Kinetic theory of gases: Assumptions, concept of pressure; Kinetic interpretation of temperature, RMS speed of gas molecules; Degrees of freedom, law of equipartition of energy (applications to specific heat capacities of gases); Mean free path, Avogadro's number

title: Gravitation
syllabus: The universal law of gravitation; Acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth; Kepler's laws of planetary motion; Gravitational potential energy; Gravitational potential; Escape velocity; Orbital velocity of a satellite; Geo-stationary satellites

title: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
syllabus: Electric potential, potential difference, electric potential due to a point charge, a dipole and system of charges; Equipotential surfaces, electrical potential energy of a system of two point charges and of electric dipole in an electrostatic field; Conductors and dielectrics, free charges and bound charges inside a conductor, dielectrics and electric polarisation; Capacitors and capacitance, combination of capacitors in series and in parallel, capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with and without dielectric medium between the plates, energy stored in a capacitor

title: Electromagnetic Waves
syllabus: Electromagnetic waves and their characteristics; Transverse nature of electromagnetic waves; Displacement current; Electromagnetic spectrum (radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays) including elementary facts about their uses; Energy density, momentum and radiation pressure of EM waves

title: Electromagnetic Induction
syllabus: Electromagnetic induction; Faraday's laws, induced EMF and current; Lenz's Law, Eddy currents; Self and mutual inductance; Motional EMF, induced electric field; AC generator

title: Electric Charges and Fields
syllabus: Electric charges: Conservation of charge, Coulomb's law: forces between two point charges, forces between multiple charges, superposition principle and continuous charge distribution; Electric field: Electric field due to a point charge, electric field lines, electric dipole, electric field due to a dipole, torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field; Electric flux, Gauss's law and its applications to find field due to infinitely long uniformly charged straight wire, uniformly charged infinite plane sheet and uniformly charged thin spherical shell

title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
syllabus: Dual nature of radiation, Photoelectric effect, Hertz and Lenard's observations; Einstein's photoelectric equation-particle nature of light; Matter waves-wave nature of particles, de Broglie relation; Davisson-Germer experiment

title: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
syllabus: Dual nature of radiation, Photoelectric effect, Hertz and Lenard's observations; Einstein's photoelectric equation-particle nature of light. Matter waves-wave nature of particles, de Broglie relation.

title: Current Electricity
syllabus: Electric current, drift velocity, mobility and their relation with electric current; Ohm's law, electrical resistance, V-I characteristics, electrical resistivity and conductivity; Temperature dependence of resistance; Internal resistance of a cell, potential difference and emf of a cell, combination of cells in series and in parallel; Kirchhoff's laws and their applications; Wheatstone bridge, Metre bridge; Potentiometer principle and its applications

title: Atoms
syllabus: Alpha-particle scattering experiment, Rutherford's model of atom; Bohr's model of hydrogen atom, energy levels, hydrogen spectrum; Expression for radius of nth possible orbit, velocity and energy of electron in his orbit; De Broglie's explanation of Bohr's second postulate of quantisation

title: Alternating Current
syllabus: Alternating currents, peak and RMS value of alternating current/voltage; Reactance and impedance; LCR series circuit, resonance; Quality factor, power in AC circuits, wattless current; AC generator and transformer

title: The Living World
syllabus: What is living? Biodiversity; Need for classification; Taxonomy & Systematics; Concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy; Binomial nomenclature

title: Structural Organisation in Animals: Tissues and Frog (Set 2)
syllabus: Animal tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, and Neural tissues; Morphology, anatomy, and physiology of Frog (Rana tigrina)

title: Structural Organisation in Animals: Animal Tissues and Frog
syllabus: Animal tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular and Neural tissues; Morphology, anatomy and functions of different systems (digestive, circulatory, respiratory, nervous, excretory and reproductive) of Frog (Rana tigrina) and Insect brief account.

title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
syllabus: Flower structure; Development of male and female gametophytes; Pollination - types, agencies and examples; Outbreeding devices; Pollen-Pistil interaction; Double fertilization; Post-fertilization events - Development of endosperm and embryo, Development of seed and formation of fruit; Special modes - Apomixis, parthenocarpy, polyembryony; Significance of seed and fruit formation.

title: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
syllabus: Energy bands in conductors, semiconductors and insulators (qualitative ideas only); Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors (n-type and p-type); p-n junction diode: I-V characteristics in forward and reverse bias; Application of junction diode as a rectifier (half-wave and full-wave rectification).

title: Respiration in Plants and Cellular Respiration
syllabus: Exchange of gases; Cellular respiration - glycolysis, fermentation (anaerobic), TCA cycle (Krebs cycle) and electron transport system (aerobic); Energy relations - Number of ATP molecules generated; Amphibolic pathways; Respiratory quotient.

title: Reproductive Health
syllabus: Need for reproductive health and prevention of sexually transmitted infections (STIs/STDs); Birth control - Need and Methods, Contraception (Natural, Barrier, IUDs, Oral pills, Injections, Implants, Surgical methods) and Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP); Amniocentesis; Infertility and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) – IVF, ET, ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI, IUI.

title: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
syllabus: Mendelian Inheritance; Deviations from Mendelism - Incomplete dominance, Co-dominance, Multiple alleles and Inheritance of blood groups, Pleiotropy; Polygenic inheritance; Chromosomal theory of inheritance; Chromosomes and genes; Sex determination (humans, birds, honey bee); Linkage and crossing over; Sex-linked inheritance (Haemophilia, Colour blindness); Mendelian disorders in humans (Thalassemia, Sickle-cell anaemia, Phenylketonuria, Cystic fibrosis); Chromosomal disorders (Down's syndrome, Turner's syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome).

title: Plant Kingdom
syllabus: Salient features and classification of plants into major groups-Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms (three to five salient and distinguishing features and at least two examples of each category)

title: Plant Growth and Development
syllabus: Seed germination; Phases of plant growth and plant growth rate; Conditions of growth; Differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation; Sequence of developmental process in a plant cell; Plant growth regulators - Auxin, Gibberellin, Cytokinin, Ethylene, and Abscisic acid (ABA).

title: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
syllabus: Photosynthesis as a means of autotrophic nutrition; Site of photosynthesis; Pigments involved in photosynthesis (elementary idea); Photochemical and biosynthetic phases of photosynthesis; Cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation; Chemiosmotic hypothesis; Photorespiration; C3 and C4 pathways; Factors affecting photosynthesis.

title: Organisms and Populations
syllabus: Organisms and Environment: Population interactions - mutualism, competition, predation, parasitism, commensalism, amensalism; Population attributes - population growth, birth rate (natality) and death rate (mortality), sex ratio, age distribution, population density, growth models (Exponential and Logistic growth).

title: Nuclei
syllabus: Composition and size of nucleus, atomic masses, isotopes, isobars; isotones. Mass-energy relation, mass defect; binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number, nuclear fission, and nuclear fusion.

title: Neural Control and Coordination
syllabus: Neuron and nerves; Nervous system in humans - Central Nervous System (Brain and Spinal Cord), Peripheral Nervous System (Somatic and Autonomic), and Visceral Nervous System; Generation and conduction of nerve impulse; Synaptic transmission.

title: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
syllabus: Morphology and modifications of root, stem, leaf, inflorescence (cymose and racemose), flower, fruit, and seed; Plant tissues (Meristematic and Permanent); Anatomy of root, stem, and leaf; Floral characters and economic importance of Families: Malvaceae, Cruciferae (Brassicaceae), Leguminosae (Fabaceae), Compositae (Asteraceae), and Gramineae (Poaceae).

title: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
syllabus: Search for genetic material and DNA as genetic material; Structure of DNA and RNA; DNA packaging; DNA replication; Central dogma; Transcription, genetic code, translation; Gene expression and regulation - Lac Operon; Genome and Human Genome Project (HGP); DNA fingerprinting; Protein biosynthesis.

title: Microbes in Human Welfare
syllabus: Microbes in household food processing; Microbes in industrial production (fermented beverages, antibiotics, chemicals, enzymes and other bioactive molecules); Microbes in sewage treatment (primary and secondary/biological treatment); Microbes in production of biogas (energy generation); Microbes as biocontrol agents; Microbes as biofertilizers.

title: Locomotion and Movement
syllabus: Types of movement - ciliary, flagellar, amoeboid, muscular; Skeletal muscle - contractile proteins and muscle contraction; Skeletal system and its functions; Joints; Disorders of muscular and skeletal system - Myasthenia gravis, Tetany, Muscular dystrophy, Arthritis, Osteoporosis, Gout.

title: Human Reproduction
syllabus: Male and female reproductive systems; Microscopic anatomy of testis and ovary; Gametogenesis - spermatogenesis & oogenesis; Menstrual cycle; Fertilisation, embryo development up to blastocyst formation, implantation; Pregnancy and placenta formation; Parturition and Lactation.

title: Human Health and Disease
syllabus: Health and Disease; Pathogens; Parasites causing human diseases (Malaria, Filariasis, Ascariasis, Typhoid, Pneumonia, Common cold, Amoebiasis, Ringworm, Dengue, Chikungunya); Basic concepts of immunology - vaccines; Cancer, HIV and AIDS; Adolescence, drug and alcohol abuse; Tobacco abuse.

title: Excretory Products and Their Elimination
syllabus: Modes of excretion - Ammonotelism, ureotelism, uricotelism; Human excretory system - structure and function; Urine formation, Osmoregulation; Regulation of kidney function - Renin-angiotensin, Atrial Natriuretic Factor, ADH and Diabetes insipidus; Role of other organs in excretion; Disorders - Uraemia, Renal failure, Renal calculi, Nephritis; Dialysis and artificial kidney.

title: Evolution
syllabus: Origin of life; Biological evolution and evidences for biological evolution from paleontology, comparative anatomy, embryology, and molecular evidence; Darwin's contribution, Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution; Mechanism of evolution - Variation (Mutation and Recombination) and Natural Selection with examples, types of natural selection; Gene flow and genetic drift; Hardy-Weinberg's principle; Adaptive Radiation; Human evolution.

title: Ecosystem
syllabus: Ecosystem - Patterns, components; Productivity (GPP, NPP, Secondary productivity) and Decomposition (Fragmentation, Leaching, Catabolism, Humification, Mineralisation); Energy flow (PAR, 10% law, food chains, food webs); Ecological pyramids - Pyramids of number, biomass, and energy.

title: Chemical Coordination and Integration
syllabus: Endocrine glands and hormones; Human endocrine system - Hypothalamus, Pituitary, Pineal, Thyroid, Parathyroid, Thymus, Adrenal, Pancreas, Gonads; Hormones of heart, kidney, and gastrointestinal tract; Mechanism of hormone action; Role of hormones as messengers and regulators; Hypo- and hyperactivity and related disorders (Dwarfism, Acromegaly, Cretinism, Goiter, Exophthalmic goiter, Diabetes mellitus, Diabetes insipidus, Addison's disease).

title: Cell: The Unit of Life
syllabus: Cell theory and cell as the basic unit of life; Structure of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell; Plant cell and animal cell; Cell envelope, cell membrane, cell wall; Cell organelles - structure and function; Endomembrane system - Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, Lysosomes, Vacuoles; Mitochondria, Ribosomes, Plastids, Microbodies; Cytoskeleton, Cilia, Flagella, Centrosome and Centrioles; Nucleus - nuclear membrane, chromatin, nucleolus.

title: Cell Cycle and Cell Division
syllabus: Cell cycle, phases of cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M phase, G0 quiescent stage); Mitosis - stages (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase), cytokinesis, significance of mitosis; Meiosis - stages (Meiosis I: prophase I, metaphase I, anaphase I, telophase I; Meiosis II), cytokinesis, significance of meiosis.

title: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
syllabus: Respiratory organs in animals (recall only); Respiratory system in humans; Mechanism of breathing and its regulation in humans - Exchange of gases, transport of gases and regulation of respiration; Respiratory volumes and capacities; Disorders related to respiration - Asthma, Emphysema, Occupational respiratory disorders.

title: Body Fluids and Circulation
syllabus: Composition of blood, blood groups (ABO, Rh), coagulation of blood; Composition of lymph and its function; Human circulatory system - Structure of human heart and blood vessels; Cardiac cycle, cardiac output, ECG, Double circulation; Regulation of cardiac activity; Disorders of circulatory system - Hypertension, Coronary artery disease, Angina pectoris, Heart failure.

title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
syllabus: Principles of Biotechnology - Genetic engineering (Recombinant DNA technology) and Maintenance of sterile/bioprocess engineering; Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology - Restriction enzymes (Exonucleases and Endonucleases), Cloning vectors (Plasmids, Bacteriophages, pBR322, Ti plasmid), Competent host (Transformation, Micro-injection, Biolistics/Gene gun); Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology - Isolation of genetic material (DNA), Cutting of DNA at specific locations, Agarose gel electrophoresis, Amplification of gene of interest using Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), Insertion of recombinant DNA into host, Obtaining the foreign gene product (Bioreactors - Stirred tank and Sparged), Downstream processing.

title: Biotechnology and its Applications
syllabus: Application of Biotechnology in health and agriculture - Human insulin and vaccine production, gene therapy; Genetically modified organisms - Bt crops (Bt cotton, Bt corn), Pest resistant plants (RNA interference); Transgenic Animals (production and reasons for creation); Biosafety issues - Biopiracy and patents, GEAC.

title: Biomolecules
syllabus: Chemical constituents of living cells: Biomolecules - structure and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids; Primary and secondary metabolites; Nature of bond linking monomers in a polymer; Dynamic state of body constituents - concept of metabolism; Metabolic basis for living; The living state; Enzymes - chemical nature, properties, mechanism of enzyme action, factors affecting enzyme activity, classification and nomenclature of enzymes, co-factors.

title: Biological Classification
syllabus: Five kingdom classification; Salient features and classification of Monera, Protista and Fungi into major groups; Lichens, Viruses, Viroids and Prions

title: Biodiversity and its Conservation
syllabus: Concept of Biodiversity (Genetic, Species, Ecological diversity); Patterns of Biodiversity (Latitudinal gradients, Species-Area relationships); Importance of Biodiversity (David Tilman's experiments, Paul Ehrlich's Rivet Popper hypothesis); Loss of Biodiversity ('The Evil Quartet' - Habitat loss and fragmentation, Over-exploitation, Alien species invasions, Co-extinctions); Biodiversity Conservation (Narrowly utilitarian, Broadly utilitarian, Ethical reasons); In-situ Conservation (Biosphere reserves, National parks, Wildlife sanctuaries, Sacred groves, Biodiversity hotspots) and Ex-situ Conservation (Zoological parks, Botanical gardens, Wildlife safari parks, Cryopreservation, Seed banks, Tissue culture); Endangered organisms, IUCN Red List / Red Data Book; International Conventions (Earth Summit and World Summit).

title: Atoms
syllabus: Alpha-particle scattering experiment; Rutherford's model of atom; Bohr model of hydrogen atom, Expression for radius of nth possible orbit, Velocity and energy of electron in nth orbit, Hydrogen line spectra (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, and Pfund series), De Broglie's explanation of Bohr's second postulate of quantization.

title: Animal Kingdom
syllabus: Salient features and classification of animals: Non-chordates up to phyla level (Porifera, Coelenterata, Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, Hemichordata) and Chordates up to classes level (Cyclostomata, Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia)

title: Work, Energy, Power & Collisions
syllabus: Work done by a constant force and a variable force, Kinetic and potential energies, Work-energy theorem, Power, Potential energy of a spring, Conservation of mechanical energy, Conservative and non-conservative forces, Motion in a vertical circle, Elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions

title: Waves
syllabus: Wave motion, Transverse and longitudinal waves, Speed of transverse and longitudinal waves, Newton's formula and Laplace's correction, Displacement relation for a progressive wave, Principle of superposition of waves, Reflection of waves, Standing/Stationary waves in strings and organ pipes, Fundamental mode and harmonics, Beats

title: Wave Optics
syllabus: Wave front and Huygens' principle, reflection and refraction of plane wave at a plane surface using wave fronts. Proof of laws of reflection and refraction using Huygens' principle. Interference, Young's double slit experiment and expression for fringe width, coherent sources and sustained interference of light, diffraction due to a single slit, width of central maximum.

title: Thermodynamics
syllabus: Thermal equilibrium, Zeroth law of thermodynamics, Concept of temperature, Heat, Work and internal energy, First law of thermodynamics, Isothermal and adiabatic processes, Isobaric and isochoric processes, Cyclic and non-cyclic processes, Second law of thermodynamics, Reversible and irreversible processes, Heat engines and refrigerators

title: Thermal Properties of Matter
syllabus: Heat, Temperature, Thermal expansion, Specific heat capacity, Calorimetry, Change of state, Latent heat, Heat transfer - Conduction, Convection, Radiation, Newton's law of cooling, Stefan-Boltzmann law, Wien's displacement law

title: Rotational Motion - 2
syllabus: Moment of inertia, Radius of gyration, Values of moments of inertia for simple geometrical objects, Parallel and perpendicular axes theorems and their applications, Equilibrium of rigid bodies, Rigid body rotation and equations of rotational motion, Comparison of linear and rotational motions

title: Rotational Motion - 1
syllabus: Centre of mass of a two-particle system, Centre of mass of a rigid body, Basic concepts of rotational motion, Moment of a force, Torque, Angular momentum, Conservation of angular momentum and its applications

title: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
syllabus: Reflection of light, Spherical mirrors, Mirror formula; Refraction of light, Total internal reflection and its applications, Optical fibres; Refraction at spherical surfaces, Lenses, Thin lens formula, Lensmaker's formula, Magnification, Power of a lens, Combination of thin lenses in contact; Refraction and dispersion of light through a prism; Optical instruments - Microscopes and Astronomical Telescopes (reflecting and refracting) and their magnifying powers.

title: Properties of Solids
syllabus: Elastic behaviour, Stress-strain relationship, Hooke's Law, Young's modulus, Bulk modulus, Modulus of rigidity, Elastic potential energy, Poisson's ratio

title: Properties of Fluids
syllabus: Pressure due to a fluid column, Pascal's law and its applications, Effect of gravity on fluid pressure, Viscosity, Stokes' law, Terminal velocity, Streamline and turbulent flow, Critical velocity, Bernoulli's principle and its applications, Surface energy and surface tension, Angle of contact, Excess pressure across a curved surface, Applications of surface tension - drops, bubbles, and capillary rise

title: Oscillations
syllabus: Periodic and oscillatory motions, Period, Frequency, Displacement as a function of time, Periodic functions, Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) and its equation, Phase, Velocity and acceleration in SHM, Force law for SHM, Energy in SHM (Kinetic and Potential energies), Simple pendulum and derivation of its time period, Oscillations of a spring (mass-spring system, series and parallel combinations), Free, forced and damped oscillations, Resonance

title: Moving Charges and Magnetism
syllabus: Concept of magnetic field, Oersted's experiment; Biot-Savart law and its application to current carrying circular loop; Ampere's law and its applications to infinitely long straight wire and solenoid; Force on a moving charge in uniform magnetic and electric fields, Lorentz force; Force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field; Force between two parallel current-carrying conductors-definition of ampere; Torque experienced by a current loop in uniform magnetic field; Current loop as a magnetic dipole and its magnetic moment; Moving coil galvanometer-its current sensitivity and conversion to ammeter and voltmeter.

title: Magnetism and Matter
syllabus: Current loop as a magnetic dipole and its magnetic dipole moment, Magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron, Magnetic field intensity due to a magnetic dipole (bar magnet) along its axis and perpendicular to its axis, Torque on a magnetic dipole (bar magnet) in a uniform magnetic field, Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid, Magnetic field lines, Magnetic properties of materials - Diamagnetic, Paramagnetic and Ferromagnetic substances with examples, Effect of temperature on magnetic properties (Curie's law and Curie temperature), Magnetization and magnetic susceptibility

title: Kinetic Theory of Gases
syllabus: Equation of state of a perfect gas, Work done on compressing a gas, Kinetic theory of gases - assumptions, Concept of pressure, Kinetic interpretation of temperature, RMS, average and most probable speeds of gas molecules, Degrees of freedom, Law of equipartition of energy and applications to specific heat capacities of gases (monoatomic, diatomic, polyatomic gases and mixtures), Mean free path, Avogadro's number

title: Gravitation
syllabus: Universal law of gravitation, Acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth, Kepler's laws of planetary motion, Gravitational potential energy, Gravitational potential, Escape velocity, Motion of a satellite, Orbital velocity, Time period and energy of a satellite

title: Electromagnetic Waves
syllabus: Electromagnetic waves and their characteristics, Transverse nature of electromagnetic waves; Electromagnetic spectrum (radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays) including elementary facts about their uses; Displacement current.

title: Electromagnetic Induction
syllabus: Electromagnetic induction; Faraday's laws, induced EMF and current; Lenz's Law, Eddy currents. Self and mutual induction, Motional electromotive force.

title: Electric Potential and Capacitance
syllabus: Electric potential, Potential difference, Electric potential due to a point charge, A dipole and system of charges; Equipotential surfaces, Electrical potential energy of a system of two point charges and of electric dipole in an electrostatic field. Conductors and dielectrics, Free charges and bound charges inside a conductor. Dielectrics and electric polarisation, Capacitors and capacitance, Combination of capacitors in series and in parallel, Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with and without dielectric medium between the plates, Energy stored in a capacitor.

title: Electric Charges and Fields
syllabus: Electric charges: Conservation of charge, Coulomb's law-forces between two point charges, forces between multiple charges; superposition principle and continuous charge distribution. Electric field: Electric field due to a point charge, Electric field lines, Electric dipole, Electric field due to a dipole, Torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field. Electric flux, Statement of Gauss's theorem and its applications to find field due to infinitely long straight wire, uniformly charged infinite plane sheet, and uniformly charged thin spherical shell (field inside and outside).

title: Current Electricity
syllabus: Electric current, Flow of electric charges in a metallic conductor, Drift velocity, Mobility and their relation with electric current; Ohm's law, Electrical resistance, V-I characteristics (linear and non-linear), Electrical energy and power, Electrical resistivity and conductivity; Temperature dependence of resistance; Internal resistance of a cell, Potential difference and emf of a cell, Combination of cells in series and in parallel, Kirchhoff's laws and simple applications, Wheatstone bridge, Metre bridge.

title: Alternating Current
syllabus: Alternating currents, Peak and RMS value of alternating current/voltage; Reactance and impedance; LCR series circuit, Resonance; Power in AC circuits, Wattless current; AC generator and transformer.

title: Units and Measurements
syllabus: Units of measurements, System of Units, SI Units, Fundamental and Derived units, Least count, Significant figures, Errors in measurements, Dimensions of Physical quantities, Dimensional analysis and its applications

title: Sequence and Series
syllabus: Arithmetic Progression (AP), Geometric Progression (GP), Harmonic Progression (HP), Arithmetic-Geometric Series (AGP), AM-GM-HM Inequalities, Telescopic Series & Special Sequences

title: NEET Practice Test: Kinematics, Current Electricity & Heating Effects
syllabus: Kinematics (Motion in a Straight Line, Motion in a Plane, Relative Motion, Graphs), Current Electricity (Ohm's Law, Drift Velocity, Cells & Circuits, Kirchoff's Laws, Measuring Instruments), Heating Effects of Current

title: Motion in a Straight Line (Kinematics Part 1)
syllabus: Frame of reference, Motion in a straight line, Position-time graph, Speed and velocity, Uniform and non-uniform motion, Average speed and instantaneous velocity, Uniformly accelerated motion, Velocity-time graph, Position-time graph, Relations for uniformly accelerated motion

title: Motion in a Plane and Vectors
syllabus: Scalars and Vectors, Vector addition and subtraction, Scalar and vector products, Unit vector, Resolution of a vector, Relative velocity, Motion in a plane, Projectile motion, Uniform circular motion

title: Laws of Motion Part 1
syllabus: Force and inertia, Newton's First law of motion, Momentum, Newton's Second Law of motion, Impulses, Newton's Third Law of motion, Law of conservation of linear momentum and its applications, Equilibrium of concurrent forces

title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions & SOT
syllabus: Inverse Trigonometric Functions (Properties, Principal Values, Equations & Inequalities), Solution of Triangles

title: Rotational Motion, Gravitation and Mechanical Properties of Solids
